pass_b_english: Cyril: …he has come unto a slave’s form, and unto a measure of humanity.
Palladius: How subtle the word and deep.
Cyril: Yet it comes not away from the aim.

Cyril: And with the ark holding thus, ‘And you will set,’ he says, ‘the golden altar unto incense opposite the ark.’ And that Christ is the golden altar, I think has been said sufficiently for us. Yet it has been set opposite the ark, upon which is the veil, and in a circle the Seraphim, and higher God, as somehow receiving the incomparable fragrance of Emmanuel. For he did not do sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth, as has been written; therefore also he himself was saying, ‘The Father loves the Son.’ And we ourselves also are acceptable to God, fragrant with Christ’s ointment. And Paul will also confirm writing: ‘And to God thanks who always triumphs us in the Christ, and who manifests the smell of his knowledge through us, because we are Christ’s fragrance to God.’

Cyril: Let us think then exactly, casting the eye into the things written, that the ark has been seated in the flank of the holy tent toward southwest and west; and opposite it the golden altar, in the place toward ray. For dawn and setting have been filled with the Christ, and north and south. And indeed a place for the lampstand, the southern things of the tent; and for the table, the things toward north. And that through both the Christ is signified, a long word has already shown beforehand for us; for that Christ is light, the lampstand makes clear; and that life and living bread, the table and the things in it. Yet think that, and observe the mystery: for most southern is the country of the Jews, and more northern again that of the nations. So then from the placing of both—I mean of the lampstand and of the table—it will somehow remain for those who wish to think very well, that to the Jews Christ shone light, and among them he was proclaiming, ‘I am the light.’ For he has been sent unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And, ‘Theirs are the promises,’ according to the Scriptures. And since they did not accept the light of the truth, he has become for the nations life and bread from heaven; and not apart from light the nations; and this also you would learn, the light of the lampstand extending also unto the northern things of the tent. And with the holy tent being most narrow, nothing unlikely that the lampstand seems all but also to have been set beside the table, even if it should have the southern place. And the type also shows for us otherwise, that when divine light shines out those worthy would be able to share Christ, as living and true bread.
